Perfume rating 4.53 out of 5 with 20,794 votes

Le Male Elixir by Jean Paul Gaultier is a Oriental Fougere fragrance for men. Le Male Elixir was launched in 2023. The nose behind this fragrance is Quentin Bisch. Top notes are Lavender and Mint; middle notes are Vanilla and Benzoin; base notes are Honey, Tonka Bean and Tobacco.

Welcome on board!
The new sailor Le Male Elixir will induce burning cravings and drive your senses crazy. Burning desire spreads with the irresistible notes of fresh lavender, warming tonka bean, and gentle benzoin. With a gilded torso, this fiery novelty from Jean Paul Gaultier embodies radiant power and seductive charisma.
It is finished! You melt away with burning desire.

This intense fragrance ignites the fire of the senses on his upper body and gives the soft skin a burning sensuality. After a refreshing breeze of mint, the tide rises to addiction, becoming a glowing elixir. In this breath of fresh air, dashing lavender quickly takes on lusty proportions, enhanced by the balsamic richness of benzoin with syrupy vanilla accents. The tonka bean trumps with its warm and sweet tones between honey and tobacco. The time has come: You jump!

Radiant at first sight, glowing with masculinity, more fiery than ever. The torso is bursting with muscles, the skin is bathed in copper color by the sinking sun. What a Gaultier body... what accomplished style. Finely chiseled grooves stand out on its muscles dipped in gold and merge with the amber stripes of the sailor shirt, which plays with transparency effects in a highly sexy way.

Available as 75ml and 125ml Parfum.

I LOVE JPG ELIXIR 12/01/25 23:51

As a non biased user, this fragrance is the best JPG, undisputed, it opens up with a minty freshness with a hint of sweetness, simmilar to that of le male le parfum, but as it dries down it becomes a more linear, sweeter scent, the sexy sweetness of vanilla and honey really shows and gives it a damp sweetness like a toffe or caramel on your nose, absolute gourmand goodness. Jean paul gaultier Le Male Elixir x ML Ramnarain Perfumers Kashmir 192121 attar

This combo layering is perfect for night weddings and evening events — rich, elegant, and beautifully layered. Le Male Elixir opens with a burst of fresh mint that cuts through the heaviness and gives the blend a clean, confident lift. As it settles, Kashmir 192121 starts sneaking in with those unexpected saffron whiffs — warm, slightly smoky, and beautifully exotic — showing up at random moments like little flashes of luxury.

The creamy woods and soft spice from the attar melt effortlessly into Elixir’s sweet amber-vanilla base, creating a smooth, sensual, and subtly dramatic scent trail.

Guys, try this out.





tommier77 11/27/25 00:55

Jean Paul Gaultier Le Male Elixir opens with a strong burst of mint that immediately feels fresh and attention-grabbing. As it settles, it shifts into a smoother, sweeter blend of vanilla, honey, and lavender, creating a warm and playful vibe. The sweetness gives it a youthful, energetic edge, making it feel very much like a younger man’s fragrance. It’s fun, confident, and easy to wear, and thanks to its smooth dry-down, it’s something I’d definitely wear on a daily basis.

I personally enjoy this fragrance despite all the hate and back lash it gets online. I do understand it has arguably better dupes for a fraction of the price. But for now, while I still have a bottle in my collection, I will continue to wear it.

ranchero 11/26/25 06:05

I cannot fathom how this fragrance gets so much positive attention. I guess most people who are into the JPG line are very young; I can see this being popular with middle schoolers. This is a sickly sweet mix of vanilla and overpowering mint, and somehow the combination lands on an oddly chocolate-like smell—just not in a good way. It’s so poorly blended that I cannot detect the other individual notes. Something about the synthetic sweetness being disrupted by the jarring mint note like that makes this smell cheap. This is also a fragrance that leans feminine because of how sweet it is.

My first impression was immediately tainted with a sense of disappointment in the fragrance community at large for hyping up something this bad. I’ve heard some people compare this to Naxos—lol, not even close. The honey note in Naxos is extremely realistic and prominent, and the sweetness is much more subtle and alluring. These fragrances share gold-colored bottles and a similar Fragrantica note profile, but that’s where the similarities end.

JPG Le Male Elixir serves as a reminder for me that nothing—absolutely nothing—is blind-buy safe. This is also why fragrance as a hobby is so fulfilling: it always keeps me guessing.

After my relationship with C-3PO ended, I thought I was done with golden man bulges forever. Little did I know that "Le Male Elixir" was waiting for me!

"Elixir" brings game! Each whiff is an olfactory orgasm that ends with a prematurely runny nose. Jean Paul Gaultier merged the saltiness of the OG with the bitchiness of an uncaffeinated Anderson Cooper. It carries on the tradition of "look inside my pants!" fragrances while appealing to a new generation of men who grew up on gangsta rap, Axe body spray, and Bridget the Midget porn films.

Can we talk about the bottle? "Elixir" utilizes the familiar "Bobby No-Limbs" design, complete with the trademark "bulge" that makes you slightly uncomfortable to own it. Jean Paul Gaultier wisely scrapped plans for a "secret" atomizer that would have spurted you with scent out of the bottle's buttocks.

All in all, "Elixir" is pretty standard "Le Male" fare.

Ryuseu 10/26/25 23:48

Bought in to the TikTok hype when it first came out because I needed a designer frag more suited for night and clubbing. Still to this day I rock Le Male Elixir from time to time when I need a dumb reach just because of how sweet, addictive and mass appealing it is.

Scent: Minty kinda fresh JPG signature opening but you can immediately smell the vanilla sweetness that the elixir boasts. After the initial freshness is where the true scent of honey and light tobacco just cascades around you. Very gourmand smelling even if it wasn’t intentional just because that honey note is so luxurious and the tobacco note is just lightly smoky to add some depth.

Performance: Long lasting and projects heavily with a beautiful sillage. It’s meant to be like an attention puller which it definitely achieves that and will be noticed by people around you due to its performance.

Versatility: This is basically a night time exclusive as I don’t think most people want to rock a honey vanilla forward fragrance in the day unless it’s moderately cold out. Most people would probably use it as a clubbing scent as it’s youthful and sweet but I definitely think older gents can rock it due to it’s depth. Masculine leaning due to that tobacco note but the ladies could still rock it confidently due to it’s sweetness and gourmand nature.

Scent: 8/10
Performance: 9/10
Versatility: 5.5/10

Personal Score: 7.5/10
Le Male Elixir’s that cool frat boy that everyone kinda likes. Fun, mass appealing and boisterous with just the lightest hint of complexity to add some character.

#1 ~My first real perfume~

I got this for Christmas 2024 from my wife. I couldn’t really wear it for months because she was pregnant and her nose became super sensitive to literally everything. So I could only test it a few times during winter and spring when I wasn’t home or was working in the office.

I still remember that opening so clearly. It was exactly the one I fell in love with the first time I smelled it in a store. Whenever we went shopping, I always sneaked off to check out perfumes after seeing so many TikTok videos, and this was the only one that really stood out, and not just from the overall palette of JPs, but from every designer fragrance, even though all of them were completely new to me!

That popcorn-ish, sweet, slightly burnt-rubber vibe in the top notes was perfect. The drydown was really sweet too, with a strong biscuit-honey tone.

When I finally got to wear it more often, summer was almost over. Still smelled amazing.
But now I’m a bit confused… It’s only been 10 months, I’ve used maybe 15 ml, and the opening seems to have changed or maybe disappeared. (?)
The lavender feels stronger now, and it’s still kind of sweet, but I’m not sure if that’s normal.

I’ve been really careful with it, stored it in a cool, dark place since it’s a precious gift. So I don’t know if it aged weirdly, or macerated the wrong way :D Or maybe my nose just changed, improved? Sometimes when I test it in stores, that perfect opening and drydown are still there, but other times I get the same thing as with mine.

Le Male Elixir opens with a slightly sharp mint note and quickly transforms into a sweet scent where vanilla and honey become very strong. What truly fascinates me about this fragrance is that, despite its sweetness, it never turns into a gourmand scent but consistently maintains its masculine and attractive, seductive character. Unlike the original Le Male, that can become cloying with overdose of vanilla and lavender, Le Male Elixir keeps its sweet, pleasant nature that everyone—men, women, kids, dogs— like.

It’s an alluring scent that doesn’t feel generic yet still appeals to the masses. Jean Paul Gaultier absolutely nailed it here. A true home run—hats off to the designer. This fragrance more than deserves the hype and definitely belongs in the Hall of Fame of the best dating fragrances. Creating such a seductive sweetness with honey and vanilla without turning gourmand is, to me, a true masterpiece. This is probably the safest blind buy you could ever make. Insanely good ragrance with strong performance. When you look at the reviews, you can see that I’m not the only one who loves it. An absolute bomb of a fragrance—totally deserves the hype.

FeelingsHaver666 10/01/25 04:41

Closer to an "entry level niche" sort of scent profile and longevity than your typical designer. Most designer fragrances tend to occupy basically the exact same sort of olfactory space - citrus, spice, "fresh out the shower" sort of vibe. Le Male Elixir is an expensive-smelling gourmand with longevity that rivals far more expensive fragrances. I gave four sprays of this on myself at around 4pm and woke up the next morning at 9am still smelling of it. For a fragrance that is under £100 for 100ml that's genuinely impressive.

The scent profile itself doesn't rival something like, say, a true niche / luxury brand like Amouage but then it's nowhere near as expensive. It's more of a simple-to-understand vanilla with a little bit of honey sweetness, but not enough to be cloying. It almost smells like spraying yourself with vanilla ice cream or something like that, but the sweetness isn't ever overwhelming.

mohammed_r37 09/08/25 22:19

I wore Le Male Elixir at exactly 8 p.m., freshly out of the shower, with about 7–10 sprays.

The first hours are magnetic. For 2–3 hours, the projection is strong and radiant, wrapping me in that sharp lavender and cool mint before the golden sweetness begins to rise. Then, as the night moved on, I expected it to retreat closer, to quiet down, but it never did. It simply transformed, smoothing itself into a glowing aura, a steady and addictive warmth of vanilla, benzoin, honey, and tobacco.

By the time 4 hours had passed and I laid down to sleep, it was still dancing around me, easily detectable with every move. The air itself seemed to move with me, leaving traces that refused to fade.

And then came the true surprise. At 8 a.m., twelve hours later, the fragrance was still alive—still surrounding me, still pulsing as though it had just settled into its most mature form. This is a parfum that doesn’t vanish; it breathes with you through the night into the morning.

After a year in my collection, it has only grown smoother and more beautiful. Darker, richer, glowing in a matte, elegant way. This is not a weak fragrance—it is a seductive elixir, lasting 10–12 hours with unwavering presence, steady projection, and an aura that never surrenders.

anlammm 08/31/25 14:58

Let’s talk about my newest acquisition: Le Male Elixir.

I’ve always had a bit of a love-hate relationship with Jean Paul Gaultier fragrances, especially the Le Beau line (the only exception being Paradise Garden, which lasted the longest on my skin and is the one I truly loved). But this one really surprised me. At first spray, I felt that familiar “weirdness” I sometimes detect in their scents, but the dry down… the dry down won me over.

I’m not super familiar with the tobacco note, but honestly, I don’t get anything here that screams tobacco. What really comes through for me is honey, tonka bean, benzoin, and especially vanilla. At the start, it has a slightly lavender-y vibe mixed with the sweetness, but then it transforms completely. On my skin, it becomes addictive, with an ultra-creamy, sweet vanilla — not that dry, faintly sweet vanilla, but truly rich and sugary, like someone sprinkled sugar on top.

Performance was also excellent. JPG and Valentino fragrances tend to last on my skin, and this one was no exception: it lasted about 12 hours. From hour 1 to 8, it was very noticeable; from 9 to 12 hours, it became more moderate, turning into a skin scent around the 11th hour.

I’ve tried many dupes and clones, but honestly, Jean Paul Gaultier fragrances are tough to replicate. None I’ve tried have come close, especially Paradise Garden — I haven’t found a faithful clone yet, and I truly love it.

THE HYPE IS DESERVED!

fragrantlyenhanced 08/24/25 06:41

This and Le Parfum are probably my favorites of everything JPG has ever released. For me, the rest simply don’t suit my taste.This one, in particular, reminds me a lot of Armani Code Absolu.. that same sweet, fizzy, warm, creamy vanilla vibe. However, it feels far more refined, less loud, yet still present.. and, of course, without any suede leather notes. It has a lot of sweetness but doesn't start smellin like a candy or cola like Code absolu did.

In terms of notes, they differ, but they share a similar way of presenting themselves over time. The opening of this fragrance starts fresh and camphor'd with a minty facet, whereas Armani Code Absolu opens with tart apple, gradually progressing to the smooth, creamy texture of tonka and vanilla while retaining warmth and sweetness. The honey'd powdery animalic sweet musk is a much better fit here for this style for vanilla fragrance, I like the suede in absolu but I always felt like it was bit daring/contradicting for a ''party'' fragrance.

Le Elixir, however, executes this much more elegantly. Its transitions are smoother and less aggressive, offering a sensual, masculine vanilla that commands attention without shouting. In terms of performance and projection, it checks every box while remaining refined, young and alluring.

Honestly, this is perfect for that setting. I own a bottle of the discontued Armani Code Absolu, but I wish I had have this one instead!

Good pick, worth the money even as a non JGP fan.
